title: Concurrency tokens: rowversion, xmin and DbUpdateConcurrencyException
summary: Optimistic concurrency the EF Core way on SQL Server, PostgreSQL and SQLite, from the exception in the log to a 409 in the API.

steps.title: A concurrency token per provider
body: In the SQL topic you wrote optimistic updates by hand: `UPDATE ... WHERE id = @id AND version = @loaded`. EF Core writes that WHERE for you once a property is a **concurrency token**. Every UPDATE and DELETE of the entity then includes the token's original value, and if no row matches, EF throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`.
```csharp fragment
// SQL Server: a rowversion column, changed by the database on every update
public class Booking
public int Id { get; set; }
[Timestamp] public byte[] RowVersion { get; set; } = [];     // or .IsRowVersion() in OnModelCreating
// PostgreSQL (Npgsql provider): map a uint to the system column xmin
public uint Version { get; set; }
modelBuilder.Entity<Booking>().Property(b => b.Version).IsRowVersion();
// Any provider, SQLite included: a column you change yourself
[ConcurrencyCheck] public int Version { get; set; }              // or .IsConcurrencyToken()

SQL Server and PostgreSQL maintain their tokens on every write; SQLite has nothing equivalent, so there you bump `Version` yourself (in the endpoint, or in a SaveChanges interceptor). The SQL EF sends looks like this:
```text
UPDATE "Bookings" SET "Note" = @p0, "Version" = @p1
WHERE "Id" = @p2 AND "Version" = @p3
RETURNING 1;

txtimeline.title: Two requests, one booking, a concurrency token
txtimeline.isolation: optimistic: no locks between load and save

rows.a:
var b = await db.Bookings.FirstAsync(x => x.Id == 12, ct);
// Version = 1
rows.note: Esme's request loads the booking. The change tracker remembers Version = 1 as the original value.

rows.b:
var b = await db.Bookings.FirstAsync(x => x.Id == 12, ct);
// Version = 1
rows.note: Support's request loads the same row, also version 1.
EF adds the token's original value to the WHERE. It matches, so the save succeeds and the version moves on.
Esme's UPDATE still says Version = 1. No row matches, and EF throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException instead of overwriting.
The endpoint answers 409; Esme's screen reloads and shows C14.

txtimeline.verdict: Without the token, the second save would have silently replaced the first.

steps.prompt: Esme and a support agent load the same booking in two contexts. The agent saves first. What does this print?
code: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=tickets.db");
steps.explain: Esme's UPDATE says `WHERE Id = 1 AND Version = 1`, but the agent already made it 2: 0 rows affected. `e.Entries` holds the entry that failed, so the app can read its current database values.

steps.title: From the exception to a 409
body: In a log it looks like this:
```text
Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbUpdateConcurrencyException: The database operation was expected to affect 1 row(s),
but actually affected 0 row(s); data may have been modified or deleted since entities were loaded.
See https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=527962 for information on understanding and handling optimistic
concurrency exceptions.
at Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Update.AffectedCountModificationCommandBatch.ThrowAggregateUpdateConcurrencyExceptionAsync(...)
at BookingEndpoints.<>c.<<MapBookings>b__0_2>d.MoveNext() in BookingEndpoints.cs:line 57
Left uncaught, that is a 500 and a lost edit. Handle it where you save:
- **Tell the client** (the usual choice for APIs): `409 Conflict`, or `412 Precondition Failed` when the version came in an `If-Match` header. The client reloads and retries.
- **Merge**: `await entry.GetDatabaseValuesAsync(ct)` gives the row as it is now; decide field by field, set `entry.OriginalValues.SetValues(dbValues)` and save again.
- **Last write wins** on purpose: reload the original values and save again. Only when overwriting is really fine.
One trap: for a web API, the token to check is the one **the client loaded**, not the one you just read from the database a millisecond ago. Copy it in before saving:
```csharp fragment
db.Entry(booking).Property(b => b.Version).OriginalValue = edit.Version;

pairs: `[ConcurrencyCheck] int Version` that the app increments

steps.prompt: Configure the token for the PostgreSQL version of the app (Npgsql provider): a `uint Version` property mapped to the system column `xmin`.
steps.explain: Npgsql maps a `uint` row-version property to `xmin`, which PostgreSQL changes on every update of the row, so the app never sets it.

steps.prompt: The PUT endpoint loads the booking, copies the client's fields onto it and saves, but stale edits still overwrite newer ones. The entity has a SQL Server `rowversion`. What is missing?
options: Setting the RowVersion original value to the one the client sent, so the UPDATE compares with what the client saw
A transaction around the load and the save
Nothing: rowversion makes this safe automatically
steps.explain: The load just read the current rowversion, so the UPDATE's WHERE always matches. Copy `dto.RowVersion` into `db.Entry(booking).Property(b => b.RowVersion).OriginalValue` before saving, and the stale edit fails as it should.

steps.title: PUT with a version check
prompt: Add `PUT /bookings/{id}` to the bookings API. The body is `{ "note": "...", "version": 1 }`, where `version` is the one the client loaded. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
- Load the booking (`FirstOrDefaultAsync(..., ct)`); 404 if there is none.
- Make EF compare with the **client's** version: set the `Version` property's `OriginalValue` to `edit.Version`.
- Set the new note and `Version = edit.Version + 1`, then `SaveChangesAsync(ct)`: **200** with the booking.
- On `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` answer **409 Conflict** and change nothing.
`Version` is already a `[ConcurrencyCheck]` property. POST and GET are given.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/bookings", new { note = "window please", version = 0 });
var dojoOk = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/1", new { note = "aisle seat", version = 1 });
DojoWeb.Status("a save with the current version responds 200", 200, dojoOk);
var dojoStale = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/1", new { note = "front row", version = 1 });
DojoWeb.Status("a save with a stale version responds 409", 409, dojoStale);
var dojoNext = await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/1", new { note = "front row", version = 2 });
DojoWeb.Status("after reloading (version 2) the save works", 200, dojoNext);
DojoWeb.Status("PUT /bookings/9 responds 404", 404, await http.PutAsJsonAsync("/bookings/9", new { note = "x", version = 1 }));
hints: Wrap `await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct)` in try/catch and return `Results.Conflict()` from the catch.
steps.explain: On SQL Server or PostgreSQL you would not bump the version yourself (the database does), and you would send it as an ETag; the rest of the endpoint is identical.
